entries.name: JavaScript
entries.note: No import: the adapter puts the stereotypes in scope before it loads the handler, the same way Tac makes @onMount available to a companion. Decorators need a runtime that transpiles them — Bun or Deno, selected with --javascript-runtime. Node rejects them at parse time and its own documentation says it will not polyfill a Stage 3 proposal.

entries.name: PHP
entries.note: No shebang: Yon appends the protocol runtime after the handler, which is what PHP needs anyway — it strips a shebang only from an entry script, and the handler is the entry script.

files.name: server/routes/orders/yon.php
files.code:
<?php
// PHP has no autoloader here, so a layer is required by path. Tachyon appends
// the protocol runtime after this file, which is what PHP needs anyway: it
// strips a shebang only from an entry script, and the handler is the entry
// script.
require_once 'server/services/orders.php';

#[Controller]
class OrdersController
{
    public static function GET(YonRequest $request): YonResponse
    {
        return YonResponse::json(json_encode(['orders' => OrderService::list()]));
    }
}

files.name: server/services/orders.php
files.code:
<?php
require_once 'server/repositories/orders.php';

#[Service]
class OrderService
{
    public static function list(): array
    {
        return OrderRepository::all();
    }
}

files.name: server/repositories/orders.php

#[Repository]
class OrderRepository
{
    public static function all(): array
    {
        return [['sku' => 'anvil', 'level' => 4]];
    }
}

entries.name: Java
entries.note: A class and methods, with no main and no imports for the protocol. Java has no JSON in its standard library and a single source file has no classpath to put one on, so Tachyon supplies Json.parse and Json.write in scope — along with the annotations, for the same reason.

entries.name: Rust
entries.note: A struct and an impl — the same shape as the service and the repository below it, and the same shape a yon.js has. Reading standard input, dispatching on the method and writing the response envelope is Tachyon’s half, appended after the file. A method the handler does not declare answers 405 on its own.
